```{r}
#loading packages
library("psych")
library("lmerTest")

#load data from multi-site study
mcdata <- read.csv("~/Downloads/Data_Multisite_Study.csv")

#recode vegtype as a factor (identifies a specific vegetable dish recipe, regardless of label condition)
mcdata$vegtype <-as.factor(mcdata$vegtype)


#subset data by school in order to standardize the vegetable selection outcome within each school

schoolAdata <- mcdata[ which(mcdata$school== "A"), ]
schoolBdata <- mcdata[ which(mcdata$school== "B"), ]
schoolCdata <- mcdata[ which(mcdata$school== "C"), ]
schoolDdata <- mcdata[ which(mcdata$school== "D"), ]
schoolEdata <- mcdata[ which(mcdata$school== "E"), ]

#calculate standardized selection outcome at each school. 
PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_A  <- scale(schoolAdata$PercentDinersChooseVeg); PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_A
PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_B  <- scale(schoolBdata$PercentDinersChooseVeg); PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_B
PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_C  <- scale(schoolCdata$PercentDinersChooseVeg); PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_C
PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_D  <- scale(schoolDdata$PercentDinersChooseVeg); PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_D
PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_E  <- scale(schoolEdata$PansPerDinerinHall_SchoolE); PercDinerChooseVeg_zscore_E
#these values are saved in data set as "PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool


#relevel the condition factor so that the health-focused condition is the reference group
mcdata$condition <- relevel(mcdata$condition, ref = "healthy")

### SELECTION OUTCOME
model1 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|school/vegtype), data=mcdata, weights = weights)
summary(model1)
# the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = 0.46, p < .001. 
# the effect of basic vs. health-focused is B = 0.21, p = .072. 
# (note: if get error when running above model, remove "school/" from the model and rerun - it is essentially redundant becuase the outcome is standardized within school already)

# "confint"" can't calculate 95% CI when using weights, so we'll use 1.96*SE for the 95% CI. 

#95% CI of difference between taste-focused and health-focused: 
1.96*.0995
# so 95% CI is 0.4616 +/- 0.1950 = [0.27, 0.66]

#95% CI of difference between basic and health-focused: 
1.96*.1149
#so 95% CI is .2087 +/- 0.2252 = [-0.02, 0.43]


#relevel the condition factor so that the basic condition is the reference group (for comparing taste-focused to basic)
mcdata$condition <- relevel(mcdata$condition, ref = "basic")

#rerun mixed model for vegetable selection outcome
model1 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|school/vegtype), data=mcdata, weights = weights)
summary(model1)
# the effect of taste-focused vs. basic is B = 0.25, p = .030.

#95% CI of difference between taste-focused and basic: 
1.96*.11537
# so 95% CI is 0.2528 +/- 0.2261 = [0.03, 0.48]



# Selection outcome effects split by school (Table S3 in SOM)

#school A
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data=schoolAdata)
summary(model6); confint(model6)
## At school A, the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = 0.89, 95% CI: [0.45, 1.32], p = .004.

#school B
schoolBdata$condition <- relevel(schoolBdata$condition, ref = "healthy")
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data=schoolBdata)
summary(model6); confint(model6)
## At school B, the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = 0.55, 95% CI: [0.25, 0.85], p = .001. The effect of basic vs. health-focused is B = 0.16, 95% CI: [-0.16, 0.49], p = .33.

#school C
schoolCdata$condition <- relevel(schoolCdata$condition, ref = "healthy")
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data=schoolCdata)
summary(model6); confint(model6)
## At school C, the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = 0.63, 95% CI: [0.11, 1.15], p = .027. The effect of basic vs. health-focused is B = -0.07, 95% CI: [-0.58, 0.41], p = .78.

#school D
schoolDdata$condition <- relevel(schoolDdata$condition, ref = "healthy")
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data=schoolDdata)
summary(model6); confint(model6)
## At school D, the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = 0.19, 95% CI: [-0.21, 0.58], p = .37. The effect of basic vs. health-focused is B = 0.40, 95% CI: [-0.00, 0.81], p = .066.

#school E
schoolEdata$condition <- relevel(schoolEdata$condition, ref = "healthy")
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data=schoolEdata)
summary(model6); confint(model6)
## At school E, the effect of taste-focused vs. health-focused is B = -0.10, 95% CI: [-0.58, 0.38], p = .68. The effect of basic vs. health-focused is B = -0.00, 95% CI: [-0.49, 0.49], p = .99.






### CONSUMPTION OUTCOME

#loading consumption data from School A
massdata <- read.csv("~/Downloads/Data_Consumption.csv")

#recode vegtype as a factor (identifies a specific vegetable dish recipe, regardless of label condition)
massdata$vegtype <-as.factor(massdata$vegtype)


# Effect of label condition on mass of vegetables SELECTED
model2 = lmer(Adj_TotalMassChosen_lbs ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data = massdata)
summary(model2)
confint(model2) #calculate 95% CI
# effect of taste-focused vs health-focused labeling on mass of vegetables selected is 4.142 lbs/day, 95% CI: [1.103, 7.272], p = .029.
# converting this to kg (divide by 2.205), it's 1.88 kg/day, 95% CI: [0.50, 3.30].


#Effect of label condition on mass of vegetables WASTED
model3 = lmer(Adj_TotalMassWasted_lbs ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data = massdata)
summary(model3)
confint(model3)
# effect of taste-focused vs health-focused labeling on mass of vegetables wasted is 0.2195 lbs/day, 95% CI: [-0.4289, 0.9618], p = .56.
# converting this to kg (divide by 2.205), it's 0.10 kg/day, 95% CI: [-0.19, 0.44].


#Effect of label condition on mass of vegetables CONSUMED
model4 = lmer(Adj_TotalMassConsumed_lbs ~ condition + (1|vegtype), data = massdata)
summary(model4)
confint(model4)
# effect of taste-focused vs health-focused labeling on mass of vegetables consumed is 3.922 lbs/day, 95% CI: [1.547, 6.588], p = .018.
# converting this to kg (divide by 2.205), it's 1.78 kg/day, 95% CI: [0.70, 2.99].


#calculating Cohen's d (effect size) for each of the above consumption outcomes
tasted <- massdata[ which(massdata$condition=='tasty'),]
healthd <- massdata[ which(massdata$condition=='healthy'),]
describe(tasted) # SD for tasty condition of selection is 4.54, waste is 1.07, consumed is 3.89
describe(healthd) # SD for healthy condition of selection is 2.79, waste is 0.86, consume is 2.76

#SDpooled for tasty vs healthy selection is: 3.7680
sqrt(((4.54*4.54) + (2.79*2.79))/2)
#cohens d is: 1.10 
4.142/3.7680
#lower 95% CI: 0.29
1.1033/3.7680
#upper 95% CI: 1.93
7.2718/3.7680

#SDpooled for tasty vs healthy waste is: .9707
sqrt(((1.07*1.07) + (.86*.86))/2)
#cohens d is: .23 
.2195/.9707
#lower 95% CI: -.44
-.4289/.9707
#upper 95% CI: .99
.9618/.9707

#SDpooled for tasty vs healthy consumption is: 3.37266
sqrt(((3.89*3.89) + (2.76*2.76))/2)
#cohens d is: 1.16 
3.922/3.37266
#lower 95% CI: .46
1.5473/3.37266
#upper 95% CI: 1.95
6.5879/3.37266



# MODERATING EFFECT OF VEGETABLE TASTINESS ON VEGETABLE SELECTION 

#relevel the condition factor so that the health-focused condition is the reference group
mcdata$condition <- relevel(mcdata$condition, ref = "healthy")


#effect of individual vegetable dish tastiness
model5 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition*RecipeDeliciousness_zscore_acrossschools + (1|school/vegtype),data=mcdata, weights = weights)
summary(model5)
# the interactive effect of taste-focused condition x individual dish tastiness is B = 0.18, p = .111. 

#confint can't calculate 95% CI when using weights, so we'll use 1.96*SE for the 95% CI.
#95% CI of taste-focused:
1.96*.1103
# so 95% CI is 0.1770 +/- 0.2162 = [-0.04, 0.39]


#effect of school-level average vegetable dish tastiness
model6 <-lmer(PercentDinersChooseVeg_zscore_withinschool ~ condition*SchoolDeliciousness_zscore + (1|school/vegtype),data=mcdata, weights = weights)
summary(model6)
# the interactive effect of taste-focused condition x average school-level dish tastiness is B = 0.32, p = .002.

#95% CI of taste-focused:
1.96*.10306
# so 95% CI is 0.3212 +/- 0.2020 = [0.12, 0.52]

# Testing for differences among schools in participants' expectations of a positive taste experience based on taste-focused labels alone (absent school context)

#relevel school with school B as the reference group (school with lowest average tastiness rating of taste-focused labels)

model= lmer(taste ~ school + (1|participant) + (1|dish), data= tasty_SuppStudyA_data); summary(model); confint(model)
# there are no significant differences among schools; range of effects is 0.02 - 0.22, all p > .134

## Expected Recipe tastiness (absent the label) from N = 301 MTurkers

#load data
recipe_expectedtaste_data <- read.csv("~/Downloads/Data_Recipes_ExpectedTaste_N=301_longform.csv")

model = lm(ExpectedTastiness~ VegRecipe, data = recipe_expectedtaste_data); summary(model)

# printing intercept (average tastiness) for each dish, except for dish 1_1, which had an average tastiness of 2.2663.
coef(model) + 2.2663
```
